vendors.name: Claude Code
vendors.description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool that operates as a fully autonomous AI developer. Available across terminal, VS Code, JetBrains, desktop, web, iOS, and Slack. Claude Code can read and write files, execute terminal commands, manage git workflows, browse the web, and coordinate multi-agent teams. With 8,600+ MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and 9,000+ plugins, it integrates with virtually any tool or service. Unique capabilities include hooks for automated validation, custom agent definitions, agent teams for parallel development, and the Agent SDK for building production AI applications. Powers everything from quick bug fixes to full-stack application development with human-in-the-loop oversight.

vendors.name: Cursor
vendors.description: AI-first code editor forked from VS Code that deeply integrates AI into every aspect of the development workflow. Features intelligent inline code completion, multi-file editing with Composer, natural language code generation, and contextual chat. Understands entire codebases through indexing and provides AI-powered code navigation, refactoring, and debugging. Strong focus on developer productivity with Tab completion that predicts next edits across multiple lines.

ratings.our_notes: Best AI-native IDE for professional developers. Tab completion is industry-leading for predicting multi-line edits. Composer enables impressive multi-file changes. However, it requires developer expertise and cannot autonomously build full applications like agentic platforms. The VS Code fork means familiar keybindings and extensions work out of the box.

vendors.notes: Cursor has become one of the most popular AI IDEs, particularly among professional developers. The Composer feature for multi-file editing is a standout. Tab completion goes beyond simple autocomplete to predict entire code blocks. Supports multiple AI model backends. Strong community and rapidly iterating on features. Main limitation compared to agentic platforms is that it requires active developer involvement for all changes.

ratings.our_notes: Solid AI IDE with the Cascade agent providing good multi-file editing capabilities. Most affordable option in the AI IDE space. The rebrand from Codeium to Windsurf brought a more polished experience. However, the ecosystem is less mature than Cursor or Claude Code, and enterprise features are limited. Good budget option for small teams.

vendors.notes: Rebranded from Codeium to Windsurf in late 2024. The Cascade agent differentiates it from pure code completion tools by offering multi-step, multi-file editing workflows. OpenAI attempted to acquire Windsurf in early 2025, indicating the value of their technology. Pricing is the most competitive in the AI IDE category.

ratings.our_notes: The most widely adopted AI coding assistant with deep GitHub ecosystem integration. Strong enterprise features including IP indemnity and fine-tuning. Inline completion is reliable and fast. However, agentic capabilities lag behind Claude Code and even Cursor's Composer. Best value at the $10/mo Pro tier for individual developers. The free tier with 2,000 completions is a solid entry point.

vendors.notes: GitHub Copilot added agent mode in 2025, allowing multi-file edits and terminal command execution within VS Code. Students and open source maintainers get Copilot Pro free. The free tier (2,000 completions + 50 chat messages/month) launched in late 2024. Enterprise tier supports fine-tuning on proprietary codebases. IP indemnity on Business and Enterprise plans provides legal protection for AI-generated code.

ratings.our_notes: Impressive for rapid prototyping and simple web apps. The browser-based approach eliminates setup friction entirely. However, significant limitations for production use: limited backend capabilities, no proper database integrations, and generated code often requires substantial refactoring for production. Best used as a starting point or for throwaway prototypes, not for building real business systems.

vendors.notes: Built on StackBlitz's WebContainers technology, which runs Node.js entirely in the browser. This is both its strength (zero setup) and limitation (constrained runtime environment). Token-based pricing means costs can be unpredictable for complex projects. Good for getting a visual prototype quickly, but generated applications typically need significant work before production deployment. No native mobile app generation.

ratings.our_notes: Good for rapid prototyping and simple applications, but significant security concerns. A 2025 audit found that 170 of 1,645 Lovable-generated apps had security vulnerabilities, including exposed API keys and insecure authentication patterns. Code is exportable and uses standard React/TypeScript, which is positive. Supabase integration provides basic backend capabilities. However, generated code often needs security hardening before production use. Use for prototyping, not production business systems.

vendors.notes: Rebranded from GPT Engineer to Lovable in 2024. Credit-based system where complexity determines consumption. Simple changes use approximately 0.5 credits while new features use 2-10 credits. Generates standard React/TypeScript code that is fully exportable. The 2025 security audit revealing vulnerabilities in 10.3% of generated apps is a significant concern for production use. Student discount available (up to 50% off). Best used as a prototyping tool with professional security review before deployment.
